headline: WEIGHT SURGERY: our forge tried to fix Qwen by hand — honest negative, shipped
lede: Demo #1493 put MIT CSAIL's weight-space programming result to the test: edit Qwen3.5-0.8B's weights with no training to break its thinking loops. Every attempt failed to reproduce — and the one run that looked like a fix turned out to be a duplicated command-line flag faking success.

notes.text: WEIGHT SURGERY demo shipped to /demos: pinned Qwen3.5-0.8B on a CPU-only llama.cpp build (this box's Metal is dead), localized the loop direction from 9,220 looping positions, cut it from layers 15/19 down_proj at 0.017%–0.98% of weights, and reported the held-out numbers and full batch log either way.

Knowledge: at a 1024-token horizon the failure is verbose non-termination, not a tight attractor — sequence-mean direction ablation leaves the model coherent but rambling longer, and even the model card's presence-penalty fix fails held-out (100% cap hits on GSM8K). MIT's fix likely needs their 32k horizon and repeat-onset localization.

Harness trap caught: an appended --presence-penalty 2.0 after the standard 1.5 appeared to terminate 12/12 practice problems; the clean single-flag rerun gave 0/12. Too-good results get re-run before they get believed (#8).

Studio plumbing learned: llama.cpp brew build SIGABRTs without Metal — build v0.3.0 with -DGGML_METAL=OFF (~200 tok/s aggregate for 0.8B); MLX needs set_default_device(cpu); HF large files need /resolve/ not /raw/ (LFS pointers); pkill is dead here — kill via ps aux | awk.
